steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on TD-MPC2, a model-based RL algorithm for learning generalist world models for continuous control from large, mixed-quality multi-task datasets. Cover the motivation from generalist models, what's missing in current embodied agents and RL, how TD-MPC2 builds on TD-MPC, and a summary of the evaluation and released resources.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Generalist models from large datasets, and the gap for embodied agents
- Why RL, and what an RL algorithm for large multi-task data needs
- TD-MPC2: relation to TD-MPC, scaling, contributions
- Evaluation, results and release

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Generalist models

  - extended to robotics, but generalist embodied agent (diverse control tasks, low-level actions, multiple embodiments, large uncurated/mixed-quality data) still elusive
  - problems: (a) assume near-expert trajectories for behavior cloning -> limits data; (b) no scalable continuous control algorithms for large uncurated data
- RL
  - ideal for extracting expert behavior from uncurated data
  - most RL algorithms single-task, per-task hyperparameters, no principled way to choose them
  - multi-task algorithm must be robust to task variation (action space dimensionality, exploration difficulty, reward distribution)
  - TD-MPC2: model-based RL, generalist world models, large uncurated data (multiple domains, embodiments, action spaces, behavior policies of all skill levels), no hyperparameter-tuning
- TD-MPC2 vs TD-MPC
  - builds on TD-MPC; local trajectory optimization in latent space of learned implicit (decoder-free) world model
  - TD-MPC family strong in prior work, but mostly single-task, little scaling
  - Figure 1: naively scaling TD-MPC -> net decrease (common in RL); scaling TD-MPC2 -> consistent improvement
  - contributions: (1) robustness via revisiting core design choices; (2) architecture for multiple embodiments/action spaces without domain knowledge
  - result: scalable, robust, single set of hyperparameters for single-task and multi-task
- Evaluation
  - \mathbf{104} tasks, 4 domains: DMControl, Meta-World, ManiSkill2, MyoSuite (Figure 1 results, Figure 2 domains)
  - high-dim state/action spaces (up to \mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{39}), image observations, sparse rewards, multi-object manipulation, musculoskeletal motor control, complex locomotion (Dog, Humanoid), wide range of difficulty
  - outperforms model-based and model-free methods, same hyperparameters (Figure 1, right); "Locomotion" and "Pick YCB" hard subsets of DMControl / ManiSkill2
  - capabilities grow with model and data size; single 317 M parameter world model on \mathbf{80} tasks (Figure 1, left)
  - release \mathbf{300} + checkpoints, datasets, code at https://tdmpc2.com
  - paper ends with lessons, opportunities, risks

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Training large models on internet-scale datasets has led to generalist models that can perform a wide variety of language and vision tasks. The success of these models is largely because of the availability of enormous datasets, and architectures that are carefully designed to reliably scale with model and data size. Researchers have recently extended this paradigm to robotics, but a generalist embodied agent that learns to perform diverse control tasks via low-level actions, across multiple embodiments, from large uncurated (i.e., mixed-quality) datasets is still an elusive goal. We think current approaches to generalist embodied agents have two problems: (a) they assume near-expert trajectories for behavior cloning, which severely limits how much data is available, and (b) there is a lack of scalable continuous control algorithms that can consume large uncurated datasets.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) is an ideal framework for extracting expert behavior from uncurated datasets. However, most existing RL algorithms are designed for single-task learning and rely on per-task hyperparameters, and there is no principled method for selecting those hyperparameters. An algorithm that consumes large multi-task datasets will invariably need to be robust to the variation between different tasks (e.g., action space dimensionality, difficulty of exploration, and reward distribution). In this work we present TD-MPC 2, which is a significant step towards this goal. TD-MPC 2 is a model-based RL algorithm designed for learning generalist world models on large uncurated datasets that are composed of multiple task domains, embodiments, and action spaces, with data coming from behavior policies that cover a wide range of skill levels, and it does not need hyperparameter-tuning.

  - scalable, robust, single set of hyperparameters

  - up to \mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{39}, images, sparse rewards, multi-object manipulation, musculoskeletal control, Dog/Humanoid locomotion

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Training large models on internet-scale datasets has led to generalist models that can perform a wide variety of language and vision tasks. The success of these models is largely because of the availability of enormous datasets, and architectures that are carefully designed to reliably scale with model and data size. Researchers have recently extended this paradigm to robotics, but a generalist embodied agent that learns to perform diverse control tasks via low-level actions, across multiple embodiments, from large uncurated (i.e., mixed-quality) datasets is still an elusive goal. We think current approaches to generalist embodied agents have two problems: (a) they assume near-expert trajectories for behavior cloning, which severely limits how much data is available, and (b) there is a lack of scalable continuous control algorithms that can consume large uncurated datasets.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) is an ideal framework for extracting expert behavior from uncurated datasets. However, most existing RL algorithms are designed for single-task learning and rely on per-task hyperparameters, and there is no principled method for selecting those hyperparameters. An algorithm that consumes large multi-task datasets will invariably need to be robust to the variation between different tasks (e.g., action space dimensionality, difficulty of exploration, and reward distribution). In this work we present TD-MPC 2, which is a significant step towards this goal. TD-MPC 2 is a model-based RL algorithm designed for learning generalist world models on large uncurated datasets that are composed of multiple task domains, embodiments, and action spaces, with data coming from behavior policies that cover a wide range of skill levels, and it does not need hyperparameter-tuning.

Our algorithm builds upon TD-MPC and performs local trajectory optimization in the latent space of a learned implicit (decoder-free) world model. The TD-MPC family of algorithms has shown strong empirical performance in prior work, but most of the successes have been limited to single-task learning and there was little emphasis on scaling. As shown in Figure 1, naïvely increasing the model and data size of TD-MPC often leads to a net decrease in agent performance, which is commonly observed in RL literature. Scaling TD-MPC 2, on the other hand, leads to consistently improved capabilities. Our algorithmic contributions, which were key to achieving this, are two-fold: (1) improved algorithmic robustness by revisiting core design choices, and (2) careful design of an architecture that can accommodate datasets with multiple embodiments and action spaces without relying on domain knowledge. The resulting algorithm, TD-MPC 2, is scalable and robust, and it can be applied to a variety of single-task and multi-task continuous control problems using a single set of hyperparameters.

We evaluate TD-MPC 2 across a total of \mathbf{104} diverse continuous control tasks spanning 4 task domains: DMControl, Meta-World, ManiSkill2, and MyoSuite. Our results are summarized in Figure 1, and the task domains are visualized in Figure 2. The tasks include high-dimensional state and action spaces (up to \mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{39}), image observations, sparse rewards, multi-object manipulation, physiologically accurate musculoskeletal motor control, and complex locomotion (e.g. Dog and Humanoid embodiments), and they cover a wide range of task difficulties. Our results show that TD-MPC 2 consistently outperforms existing model-based and model-free methods, using the same hyperparameters across all tasks (Figure 1, right). “Locomotion” and “Pick YCB” here are particularly challenging subsets of DMControl and ManiSkill2. We also show that agent capabilities increase with model and data size, and we successfully train a single 317 M parameter world model to perform \mathbf{80} tasks across multiple task domains, embodiments, and action spaces (Figure 1, left). We publicly release \mathbf{300} + model checkpoints, datasets, and code for training and evaluating TD-MPC2 agents to support open-source science, available at https://tdmpc2.com. At the end of the paper we give an account of the lessons, opportunities, and risks associated with large TD-MPC 2 agents.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Training large models on internet-scale datasets has led to generalist models that perform a wide variety of language and vision tasks [1,2,3]. The success of these models can largely be attributed to the availability of enormous datasets, and to carefully designed architectures that reliably scale with model and data size. While researchers have recently extended this paradigm to robotics [4,5], a generalist embodied agent that learns to perform diverse control tasks via low-level actions, across multiple embodiments, from large uncurated (i.e., mixed-quality) datasets remains an elusive goal. We argue that current approaches to generalist embodied agents suffer from (a) the assumption of near-expert trajectories for behavior cloning, which severely limits the amount of available data [4,6,7,8,9,5], and (b) a lack of scalable continuous control algorithms that are able to consume large uncurated datasets.

Reinforcement Learning (RL) is an ideal framework for extracting expert behavior from uncurated datasets. However, most existing RL algorithms [10,11] are designed for single-task learning and rely on per-task hyperparameters, with no principled method for selecting those hyperparameters [12]. An algorithm that can consume large multi-task datasets will invariably need to be robust to variation between different tasks (e.g., action space dimensionality, difficulty of exploration, and reward distribution). In this work, we present TD-MPC 2, a significant step towards this goal. TD-MPC 2 is a model-based RL algorithm designed for learning generalist world models on large uncurated datasets composed of multiple task domains, embodiments, and action spaces, with data sourced from behavior policies that cover a wide range of skill levels, and without the need for hyperparameter-tuning.

Our algorithm, which builds upon TD-MPC [13], performs local trajectory optimization in the latent space of a learned implicit (decoder-free) world model. While the TD-MPC family of algorithms has demonstrated strong empirical performance in prior work [13,14,15,16,17,18,19,20], most successes have been limited to single-task learning, with little emphasis on scaling. As shown in Figure 1, naïvely increasing the model and data size of TD-MPC often leads to a net decrease in agent performance, as is commonly observed in RL literature [21]. In contrast, scaling TD-MPC 2 leads to consistently improved capabilities. Our algorithmic contributions, which have been key to this, are two-fold: (1) improved algorithmic robustness by revisiting core design choices, and (2) careful design of an architecture that can accommodate datasets with multiple embodiments and action spaces without relying on domain knowledge. The resulting algorithm, TD-MPC 2, is scalable, robust, and can be applied to a variety of single-task and multi-task continuous control problems using a single set of hyperparameters.

We evaluate TD-MPC 2 across a total of \mathbf{104} diverse continuous control tasks spanning 4 task domains: DMControl [22], Meta-World [23], ManiSkill2 [24], and MyoSuite [25]. We summarize our results in Figure 1 and visualize the task domains in Figure 2. Tasks include high-dimensional state and action spaces (up to \mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{39}), image observations, sparse rewards, multi-object manipulation, physiologically accurate musculoskeletal motor control, complex locomotion (e.g. Dog and Humanoid embodiments), and cover a wide range of task difficulties. Our results demonstrate that TD-MPC 2 consistently outperforms existing model-based and model-free methods, using the same hyperparameters across all tasks (Figure 1, right). Here, “Locomotion” and “Pick YCB” are particularly challenging subsets of DMControl and ManiSkill2, respectively. We further show that agent capabilities increase with model and data size, and we successfully train a single 317 M parameter world model to perform \mathbf{80} tasks across multiple task domains, embodiments, and action spaces (Figure 1, left). In support of open-source science, we publicly release \mathbf{300} + model checkpoints, datasets, and code for training and evaluating TD-MPC2 agents, available at https://tdmpc2.com. We conclude the paper with an account of the lessons, opportunities, and risks associated with large TD-MPC 2 agents.
